page: OVHcloud i1-45 is a storage-optimized virtual server instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is provisioned with 8 dedicated x86_64 physical cores (8 vCPUs without hyperthreading) based on the Intel Haswell architecture running at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The instance is allocated 45.0 GB of RAM, equating to roughly 5.62 GB per core. For I/O requirements, it bundles 1950 GB of NVMe SSD local storage (structured as 1900 GB NVMe alongside 50 GB SSD space), 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and does not include GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements reflect the generational limits of the Haswell CPU combined with non-hyperthreaded physical cores. The instance registers weak single-core metrics, scoring 939.0 on Geekbench single-core and 1120.5 on stress-ng single-core tests. Single-threaded gzip compression (18.74 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (7.31 GB/sec) both place in the bottom 10%. However, multithreaded capacity shows steady mid-tier capability due to dedicated core resources, achieving an average rating with 8940.1 in stress-ng multi-core and 4761.0 in Geekbench multi-core. PassMark CPU tests return an overall score of 9710.85, supported by basic AVX, AES, and BMI2 instruction support, though lacking AVX-512 extensions.

Memory and operational throughput maintain stable midrange ratings, recording uncached memory read bandwidth of 64.85 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 34.08 GB/sec. The instance handles in-memory and database workloads effectively, achieving 10.09 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 4441.64 in PassMark database operations. Web serving throughput registers at 7.45 GB/sec, while LLM inference benchmarks exhibit mixed mid-to-low tier tokens per second due to the absence of modern matrix acceleration instruction sets.

The primary tradeoff of the OVHcloud i1-45 is between dated single-thread compute efficiency and high storage capacity. It provides cost-effective access to nearly 2 TB of high-speed local NVMe storage coupled with substantial memory. Consequently, this server is suitable for intermediate storage-centric systems, local caching tiers, NoSQL data stores, self-hosted relational databases, and disk-intensive indexing or ETL processes that do not rely on modern vector extensions or ultra-low latency compute.

The network baseline throughput is rated at 1 Gbps without dedicated GPUs. In benchmarks, the older CPU architecture produces weak single-core metrics, including 939.0 in Geekbench single-core and lower-tier compression figures. Nonetheless, multi-core throughput, uncached memory bandwidth (64.85 GB/sec read, 34.08 GB/sec write), and database operations deliver balanced mid-tier results, with Redis SET operations achieving 10.09 million ops/sec. Balancing modest processing speeds against large NVMe storage volume and memory density, the i1-45 fits data stores, database operations, caching nodes, and local data-processing pipelines.
